back: Rising opportunity cost: each extra unit of a good costs more of the other good.
Constant opportunity cost: resources are equally suited to both goods.
Falling opportunity cost as more of a good is produced.

front: Why is the usual PPC concave?
back: Resources are not equally suited to every good, so switching less suitable resources raises the opportunity cost.

front: Name three causes of an outward shift of the PPC.
back: More resources (discovery, investment, immigration), better-quality resources (education, health), better technology.

front: Name three causes of an inward shift of the PPC.
back: Natural disasters (drought, cyclone), emigration of skilled workers, war, land degradation or disease.

front: Does a fall in unemployment shift the PPC?
back: No. It moves the economy from inside the curve towards it.

front: What does an outward shift of the PPC mean for growth?
back: Potential output has risen; actual growth happens only if the extra capacity is used.

front: How is better technology in only one industry shown?
back: The PPC pivots outwards along that good's axis only.
